problem: If $sin⁡\theta =\frac{5}{6}$ and ${90}^{∘}<\theta <{180}^{∘}$ then what is the value of $cos⁡\theta ?$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/f6c2b0f2e6b8c9b10de0341a73d8c7d1d88ba64bd046e82fee8db37828ca2555.png)

We're given that $sin⁡\theta =\frac{5}{6}.$ We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{5}{6}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{5}{6})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{25}{36}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{11}{36}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{11}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is negative in the second quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{11}}{6}.$
